reviewedFrom: docs/books-revenue-recognition.md §4a, §4b, §4c and the §5 worked example (cost-to-cost percentage of completion). Expected balances are independent of the implementation; amounts are integer cents. Pending licensed-CPA review (B16.3).

second-contract-separately-owned.derivation: Contract A (fixed price, $1,000,000, EAC $800,000) has $200,000 of its own cost: 25% complete, $250,000 earned, billed $300,000 so $50,000 over-billed. Contract B (time and materials, $200,000, EAC $250,000) has $100,000 of its own cost: 40% complete, $80,000 earned, billed $80,000 so even. B is a loss contract: total expected loss $50,000, of which $20,000 is already incurred (cost $100,000 less earned $80,000), so the reserve is $30,000, on B alone. A's profit does not absorb B's loss. A single project-wide position is refused. Ledger: revenue $330,000 = A + B; job cost $300,000; loss provision $30,000; 2350 nets billings $380,000 against earned $330,000 = $50,000 credit. Live contract value is both contracts together ($1,200,000), not whichever row comes first.

expected.projectScopeRefused: This project has more than one contract; prepare WIP for each contract

shared-cost-allocation.derivation: Three contracts. Cost code 01-500 (general conditions, $50,000) is on both A's and B's schedule of values, so its cost belongs to neither until a reviewed split; it blocks A and B, not C. Invoice SH-IU names no contract, so every contract's billings are uncertain and it blocks all three. A split that does not total 100% is refused. Assigning SH-IU to B succeeds once; a second assignment is refused. Splits are append-only. A 60/40 split is prepared and reviewed; a later 50/50 split changes the evidence, so close is refused until re-prepared and re-reviewed. Final costs: A $200,000 + $25,000 = $225,000; B $100,000 + $25,000 = $125,000; C $10,000 — together exactly the $385,000 incurred. Earned: A 225,000/800,000 × 1,000,000 = $281,250; B 125,000/180,000 × 200,000 = $138,888.888… → $138,888.89; C 10,000/80,000 × 100,000 = $12,500.

late-bill-after-review-blocks-close.derivation: A cost approved after WIP review changes the reviewed position, so close must refuse until WIP is re-prepared and re-reviewed; then 400k/800k=50% -> 500k.

revised-and-reverted-eac.derivation: earned-to-date = cost-to-date / EAC x contract; delta = earned-to-date - prior recognized (docs/books-revenue-recognition.md §4c). 200k/800k=25% -> 250k; 600k/1,000k=60% -> 600k (delta 350k); 600k/800k=75% -> 750k (delta 150k).

completed-job-carryforward.derivation: cost-to-date equals EAC -> 100% complete -> full contract recognized; a carried-forward period with no activity recognizes nothing (§4c: a run with nothing to recognize posts nothing).

wip-recognition-close-populations-agree.derivation: July is prepared and reviewed for the single-contract job. A second contract effective July 15 then changes July's population to two contracts, so the WIP check fails naming both and close is refused. Each contract is prepared and reviewed; close recognizes A 200,000/800,000 × 1,000,000 = $250,000 and B 40,000/160,000 × 200,000 = $50,000, every recognition line carrying its contract. A second job closes July as a single-contract project ($250,000 recognized with no contract), then gains a contract effective August 10; August close is refused because that revenue belongs to no contract and splitting it silently would recognize it twice.

expected.legacyClose: Revenue on WIP-01 legacy revenue — custom home was recognized before it had more than one contract, so it belongs to no contract. Reclassify that revenue to its contracts before recognizing each contract's revenue.
